evidence.text: And it is related of some of the early generations that he used to read it: (and enter among My servant, and enter My Paradise) (3).

Ahmad ibn Yusuf told me, he said: al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qatta, from Ibn Abbas, that he read it: (and enter among My servant), in the singular (4).

Khallad ibn Aslam told us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl told us, from Harun al-Qari, he said: Hilal told us, from Abu Shaykh al-Huna'i [in the reading of Ubayy] (5): (and enter among My servant); and in the saying of al-Kalbi: (and enter among My servant).

notes.en: Sīrat Ibn Hishām, 1/7, reads “ʿĀd, son of ʿAwṣ ibn Iram,” identifying Iram as ʿĀd’s ancestor, as the author does in introducing the report. Al-Qurṭubī, 20/44–45, also cites Ibn Isḥāq: “ʿĀd was son of Iram.” On that view Iram is ʿĀd’s father; on the first view it is his ancestor. Ibn Isḥāq says Sām ibn Nūḥ had children including Iram ibn Sām, from whom came the Amalekites, Pharaohs, tyrants, oppressive kings, and sinners.
